docs.liveCards.component: THE SAME DESK WITH CARDS IN FRONT OF TWO PEOPLE — the one thing a mechanic cannot be tried against on a single screen, while Live/Chess is the same shared desk with a board.
Its own section and not a scene under Mechanics, because it is not a mechanic. Everything on
this page is the magnetism page's, unchanged and imported rather than restated: what is added
here is a second pair of eyes, and every seam it needs exists so that adding them changes
docs.liveCards.scene: LIVE — one desk, two screens, and neither of them is the truth.
Everything the page above does, with the one difference that decides whether any of it was
really built: the board is somewhere else. Drag a card on the top screen and let go near an
area — it goes in, and it goes in on the bottom screen too, because what moved was the board
they share and not the picture in front of you.
A finger PROPOSES. A drop resolved on one screen alone would be real for one pair of eyes and
would never have happened for the other, so the move goes to the board everybody shares and the
authoritative answer comes back to everyone — including the seat that sent it. Turn the latency
up and watch the two halves of that: the card lands under your own finger at once (position is
reversible, so predicting it is safe) and appears on the other screen when the word arrives.
EVERY SEAT SEES EVERY CARD. Hiding is a real thing and the kit does it, but it is a second
subject, and a page teaching two at once teaches neither: with cards hidden, a reader watching
one screen cannot tell "they have not moved" from "they moved something I may not see".
AND EVERY HAND IS ON THE DESK, in its own colour — a ring on what somebody else is holding, and
a cursor wherever their finger is. The cursor is drawn even when they hold nothing, because a
hand you cannot see is a player who has left.
The two screens are two SCENES, not one drawn twice: two hosts, two clocks, two cameras, because
that is what two devices are. The far seat sits opposite and sees the desk from there — a player
who had to read their own area upside down would be reading somebody else's table.
docs.liveCards.avatars: CARDS WITH THE PEOPLE ON THE DESK — and a hand each, standing where its owner stands.
Every other live scene shows what somebody's hand is doing and nothing about the person doing
it: the cursor appears when they move and is gone the moment they stop, so a desk with a quiet
second player is a desk with one player at it. The disc is the permanent half of that message,
and where it stands is read out of that reader's own camera.
And the hand follows the person. Deal to yourself and to the other player — take a card off the
deck and let it go over either patch: it goes in, on both screens, and the patch grows to hold
it. Drag your own disc and your hand travels with it, changing sides when the side it was on
Tap your own disc and the hand shuts. It is washed in its owner's colour, and from the other
screen it stops answering: a card let go of over it comes back, and a card lying in it cannot
be picked up at all. From its OWN screen nothing has changed, because the lock is about
Turn the avatars knob off and the desk is the scene above — no people, and therefore no hands.
